texts.preamble: Harish Kumar Rijwani vs The State Of Madhya Pradesh on 6 February, 2018 The High Court Of Madhya Pradesh Mcrc-4374-2016 (Harish Kumar Rijwani Vs The State Of Madhya Pradesh) 4 Jabalpur, Dated : 06-02-2018
texts.facts: The prosecution case, in brief, is that on 23.11.2000 the Senior Food Inspector inspected the firm of the petitioner, namely, Ballarmal sh Khattumal situated in Mukadamganj, District Jabalpur wherein the e samples of 'Maida', 'Suji' and 'Atta' were taken. After taking the ad sample of 600 gms. of 'Maida', it was divided into three parts. One Pr sample was sent for Food Analysis. The report of the Analyst received in which the food item-'Maida' was found to be misbranded and of a hy sub-standard, which is an offence under sections 2 & 7 read with section 16 of the Food Adulteration Act. Complaint was filed on ad 19.3.2002 by the Food Inspector before the Judicial Magistrate First M Class, Jabalpur. The respondent No.2 is the manufacturer of 'Maida' which was being sold in sealed packet. The respondent No.3 is the of nominated person on behalf of respondent No.2. rt 2. According to the petitioner, the trial is in progress before ou the Special Court, Jabalpur under the Municipalities Act. The present petition has been filed under section 482 of the Code of Criminal C Procedure to invoke the extraordinary jurisdiction of this Court and for h quashing of the criminal case No.607/2002 pending before the Judicial ig Magistrate First Class, Jabalpur. H 3. It is stated that the sample was taken on 23.11.2000 and the report was received on 25.1.2001. However, charge-sheet has been filed on 19.2.2002, after a period of one year of the receiving of the report from the Analyst. It is also contended that the petitioner has not been informed about the report of the Food Analyst. It is mandatory under section 13(2) of the Food Adulteration Act, 1954 to inform the accused about the report.
texts.arguments: The provision of section 13(2) of the Food Adulteration Act provides as under:- "13. Report of public analyst:- Harish Kumar Rijwani vs The State Of Madhya Pradesh on 6 February, 2018 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/71894513/ 1 (2) On receipt of the report of the result of the analysis under sub-section (1) to the effect that the article of food is adulterated, the Local (Health) Authority shall, after the institution of prosecution against the persons from sh whom the same of the article of food was taken and the person, if any, whose name, address and other particulars have been disclosed under section 14A, e forward, in such manner as may be prescribed, a copy of the report of the result ad of the analysis to such person or persons, as the case may be, informing such Pr person or persons that if it is so desired, either or both of them may make an application to the court within a period of ten days from the date of receipt of the a copy of the report to get the sample of the article of food kept by the Local hy (Health) Authority analysed by the Central Food Laboratory."
